exposure: Maternal characteristics (according to Modified Robson's Criteria)
Indications for cesarean delivery (e.g., non-reassuring CTG, failed induction of labor, previous cesarean delivery)
outcome: Distribution of cesarean sections across Robson's Criteria groups
cohort: The study participants were 3,925 women who delivered in the obstetric units of Shalamar Teaching Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, between October 1st, 2022, and September 30th, 2023.
finding: The overall cesarean section rate was 73.5%, with Group 5 (previous cesarean delivery, single, cephalic, >=37 weeks) being the major contributor, accounting for almost 50% of all cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: The study found a very high cesarean section rate of 73.5%, with specific Robson's groups identified as major contributors to this mode of birth.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from delivery records spanning October 1st, 2022, to September 30th, 2023.
gest_age: Included >=37 weeks for Robson's Group 5, but no general gest_age range for the whole cohort is specified.
